It is an award scheme that: Identifies talent and supports the career advancement of researchers in the Global South Funds innovative social development projects implemented by NGOs that benefit marginalised groups in the developing world THEME - 2026 EDITION Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) for Peace and Human Security Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) are often viewed as the "hardware" of development - the tools, laboratories, and digital infrastructures that drive economic growth. However, the ultimate impact of STI on human lives is determined by the "software" of society: the institutions, capabilities, and diplomatic relations that govern how knowledge is created and shared. This edition sought to explore the role of the social sciences in, on, and for STI. We looked beyond the tools themselves to the human systems that surrounded them. Centred on the Japanese guiding principle of “Human Security”, defined as freedom to live in dignity and from fear and want, this call invited proposals that demonstrated how STI ecosystems could be shaped to foster peace, build human capability, and protect the most vulnerable through cross-border cooperation and Science Diplomacy. The Japanese Award for Outstanding Research on Development (ORD) - Click to learn more We invited research proposals that pushed the frontiers of how social sciences interacted with Science, Technology, and Innovation in the Global South and how they related to Human Security. We particularly welcomed practice-oriented research that recognised Human Security as not only a conceptual framework but also an operational agenda. We encouraged research proposals that explored the institutional, governance, and capability-building dimensions of strengthening systems that protected people from threats, as well as those that empowered individuals and communities to respond to threats themselves. Below are the finalists who will present their projects to a jury at the 2026 Global Development Conference: CHARINA CHAZALI, AKATIGA Institution, Indonesia Hazard-Ready Communities: Citizen Science, Science Diplomacy, and Community-based Governance on Technological Risk in Indonesia’s Energy Transition HYGOR PIAGET MONTEIRO MELO, University of Fortaleza, Brazil Cooling the City: Urban Trees, Public Health and Human Security for Heat Mitigation in Fortaleza THIERRY MESSIE PONDIE, University of Buea, Cameroon Leveraging Digital Startups for Peace and Human Security: Micro-Level Evidence from Conflict-Affected Communities in Cameroon The Japanese Award for Most Innovative Development Project (MIDP) - Click to learn more We invited NGOs that were using innovation not just to deliver services, but to build human capabilities among the most vulnerable and marginalised groups. We moved beyond the deployment of “tech tools” to focus on projects that empowered communities to understand, adapt, and leverage STI for their own security and dignity.
